keep: The idea is named up front: the charger holds a set voltage per cell through bulk, topping and float, and the setting sits in a narrow band with harm on both sides.

One picture carries the lesson: the set-point slider with the cited bands marked (float 2.23 to 2.27, boost 2.33 to 2.40, gassing 2.40, equalise 2.50), the two direction-only meters, the cell stepper and the temperature slider.

Worked numbers from the rule: 12 × 2.25 = 27 V (recall), 24 × 2.23 = 53.52 V, 55 × 2.23 = 122.65 V, 2.25 − 0.030 = 2.22 V at 35 °C and 2.28 V at 15 °C, and the maker's own rule giving 2.215 V a cell and 121.8 V for 55 cells at 35 °C.
Each named slip has a DO screen with a hint per wrong pick: higher is better (7), boost left on (9), the temperature sign (11), and the nominal or rested voltage used as the setting (1, 5).
Every number has a kind: 100 Ah, 10 A, 2.35 V, 4 A and 51.60 V are worded as examples; the bands, 25 °C, 20 °C, 3 mV and 3 to 5 per cent are cited; the rest are computed.
The charger stays a box: its inside is left to Electronics, gas to lesson 5 and uneven cells to lesson 6.
fix: Causal step skipped: why too high corrodes the positive grid. Say what the current a full cell cannot use does: with little sulphate left, it works on the lead grid that holds the positive plate, as one way to picture it.
Causal step skipped: why a warm cell needs a lower setting. Add, as one way to picture it, that a warm cell reacts more readily, so the same volts push more current into it.
Causal step skipped: why the setting is chosen per cell. Say each cell's band is set by its own chemistry, and series cells add their volts.
Talks about the idea instead of teaching it: 'Temperature moves the pin too' uses 'pin' with no meaning in the text. Say 'moves the band'.
The example charge setting 2.35 V a cell floats free. Say it sits inside the 2.30 to 2.45 V a cell that charge settings range over, and list both figures.
Long sentence: 'The current now falls by itself, because the cell is saturating: with less sulphate left...' runs to 25 words with a colon. Split it.
Unfinished phrase: 'Sealed cells tolerate overcharge less and have their own.' Say 'their own figures'.
Screen 12's hint for 'nothing' reads as an absolute. Say 2.15 V a cell is below the float band, so the cells are not kept full.

shape.ruleInWords: yes: charger volts = volts per cell × number of cells; float sits a little above the rested 2.1 V; warmer, lower by 3 mV a cell per degree
shape.workedExampleWithRealNumbers: yes (24 cells: 53.52 V; 55 cells at 35 °C by the maker's rule: 121.8 V)
shape.misconceptionShownFailing: yes: higher is better (screen 7), boost left on (screen 9), the temperature sign (screen 11), nominal or rested voltage as the setting (screens 1 and 5)
shape.analogyWithBreaks: yes: tyre pressure, one figure per tyre, harm on both sides, checked cold; breaks because a tyre holds still while a charger pushes current all the time
shape.putItIntoPractice: yes: ventilation first, steps, rule of thumb, worked example, mistakes

sevenFaults.falseAbsolutes: one hint, fixed above; 'every cell takes the same current' holds for cells in series
sevenFaults.briefShowsOnlyEffect: no: the meters move because of the set point held, the cause
sevenFaults.checksTestRecall: no: each DO applies the rule (multiply, correct, predict); the recall opener is the brief's
sevenFaults.thinResearch: no: eleven sources, eight added from the course notes and checked by sources.mjs (9 of 9 ok)
sevenFaults.talksAboutIdea: one phrase ('moves the pin'), fixed above
